sections.text:
Yahya, peace be upon him, is the miraculous son of the Prophet Zechariah. God created him in response to his father’s prayer to be an inheritor of prophecy and a caller to the truth.

God gave him wisdom and a deep understanding of the Torah while he was still a young child. The Almighty said: “O Yahya, take the Book firmly. And We gave him judgment as a child.”

Yahya was kind to his parents, tender-hearted, cried often out of fear of God, and lived an ascetic life away from luxury and play. Rather, he used to wear coarse clothes and eat from plants of the earth.

God commissioned him to command the Children of Israel with five words: to worship God and not associate anything with Him, to pray, to fast, to give alms, and to remember God frequently.

Yahya was brave and did not fear, for God's sake, the blame of a critic. He spoke the truth before kings and tyrants.

During his reign, there was a mighty king in Palestine called Herod, who was an unjust ruler who followed his own desires and whims.

This king wanted to marry his beautiful niece, and this marriage was forbidden in the law of the Torah in which they believe.

The king came to ask Yahya to ask Yahya about his marriage, thinking that Yahya would be courteous to him for fear of his oppression and power.

But Yahya, peace be upon him, issued a fatwa with all firmness and force that this marriage was invalid and forbidden, and he refused to change God’s rulings for the sake of the whims of kings.

Yahya's fatwa spread among the people, which aroused the king's anger and hatred, but he feared Yahya because of his status among the people.

As for the girl and her cunning mother, they felt extremely angry at Yahya’s fatwa that stopped the marriage, so they hatched a malicious and vengeful plot.

On the king's birthday, a loud party was held. The girl dressed up, entered the king, and danced for him until he admired her and captured his heart.

The king asked her to ask for whatever she wanted, and he promised her in front of those present that he would fulfill her request even if it were half his kingdom!
The girl went to her mother and asked her what she wanted, and the spiteful mother said: “Ask for the head of Yahya bin Zakaria!”

The girl returned to the king and said: “I want the head of Yahya bin Zakaria in a golden basin!”

The tyrant king agreed, and sent his soldiers, who killed the Prophet Yahya while he was standing and praying in the mihrab, and cut off his honorable head.

The head was brought in a golden basin and presented as a gift to that girl and her mother. Yahya, peace be upon him, was martyred in defense of the truth and steadfastness in his principles.

God honored him in the Qur’an with peace on the day he was born, the day he died, and the day he is resurrected alive, so that he remains a symbol of steadfastness in principles no matter the cost, and his story continues to inspire believers throughout the ages.
